hook: The paper stays the same, but a famous name changes how people read it.
readerPromise: Investigate the necessary shortcuts of scientific trust and the point where reputational signals exceed their evidential role.
protectedRevelations: Later case outcomes and research-assessment reform prescriptions
visualPlan: Keep the identical manuscript while its associated credibility signals become visible.
Use the editor’s queue to establish time pressure without caricaturing negligence.
Retain direct inspection of the work and one concrete checking step; remove repeated prestige changes.
End with the manuscript open and the verdict unresolved, inviting the reader to inspect its journey.

authorReview.scope: Complete eight-sentence script checked against canonical short-reader opening evidence for premise, clear identity, specific interest and protected revelations.

notes: Removed borrowed-authority abstraction and unnecessary fictional name. Retained reputation’s legitimate role in scarce attention and distinguished noticing work from verifying it.
Every spoken sentence independently checked against the canonical English source for clear purpose, intended viewer response, source fidelity and natural spoken wording.
All scenes remain compact, with one sentence per clip and specific restrained delivery directions. Viewer responses are editorial intentions, not results from audience testing.

sentenceIntentions.text: The paper stays the same, but a famous name changes how people read it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Expose credibility transfer through an unchanged paper.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel the oddness of a social change affecting judgment of identical work.

sentenceIntentions.text: Borrowed Credibility examines how reputation travels through science, sometimes faster than evidence.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the book and central mechanism.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand that this is about scientific reputation and evidence.

sentenceIntentions.text: A manuscript reaches busy editors who cannot check everything in equal depth.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give evaluators a fair reason to use shortcuts.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize limited time rather than assume universal corruption.

sentenceIntentions.text: Names, universities, and journals help them decide where to spend their attention.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name the familiar signals being studied.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See how prestige enters an ordinary review decision.

sentenceIntentions.text: Those shortcuts can be useful, yet they do not change the experiment behind the paper.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: State the distinction that rewards watching.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand why a helpful signal is not new experimental support.

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows what happens when attention brings citations, funding, and still more attention.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Wonder whether repeated attention has become mistaken for confirmation.

sentenceIntentions.text: It asks how research can earn trust without making every reader start from zero.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Keep the problem constructive and realistic.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Expect a serious account of trust under practical constraints.

sentenceIntentions.text: When should a respected name give way to evidence?
sentenceIntentions.purpose: End with a useful question for science readers.
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to know when direct evidence should outweigh prestige.
